Trajectory: iter-1 SSIM 0.8611 hr 0.0 (blend 0.3, factor 0.55); iter-2 SSIM 0.8644 hr EXACTLY 0.0 (blend 0.3->0.5) -- the FBP/RAM blend coefficient is EXHAUSTED: raising the FBP fraction lifted raw SSIM marginally (+0.003) but did NOT move calibrated headroom off 0.0, so on the RMSE-sensitive metric RAM is at/below the LD-FBP floor (baseline 0.8078, oracle HD-FBP 0.9331) regardless of blend. Failure mode: RAM is a pretrained zero-shot deepinv recon that never saw real LDCT helical-rebinned fan data; its denoiser adds no recoverable signal over FBP on dense (2304-view) rebinned Mayo -> FBP-bounded. ONE knob NOT yet probed = ram_factor (physics.factor, solver_ram.py L348), the operator-gain used in RAM's prox_l2 data-consistency realign step (L20: 0 = skip prox_l2). It is the most DIAGNOSTIC remaining RAM hyperparameter: blend mixes FBP vs RAM linearly AFTER inference, whereas ram_factor changes RAM's INTERNAL DC step -- the actual mechanism by which RAM is supposed to add signal over its FBP init. Lower it 0.55->0.2 (toward the skip-prox_l2 limit) to isolate whether weakening RAM's DC realign moves the metric at all. Hypothesis: RAM is structurally FBP-bounded on dense Mayo -- the prox_l2 strength does not matter because RAM's prior carries no LDCT-specific signal. Falsifier: if hr at ram_factor=0.2 != 0.0 (rises OR drops), RAM's internal DC step DOES matter and RAM is not purely FBP-bounded; if hr stays flat at 0.0 across both the post-hoc blend (iter-2) AND the internal prox_l2 gain (iter-3), RAM is CONFIRMED structurally FBP-bounded on dense Mayo -> FILE NEGATIVE RESULT, STOP iterating this solver. Budget: only a scalar physics.factor changes -> zero added compute vs iter-2 (which ran 1100.9 s = 18.3 min for 214 single forward passes + one op-norm power iter), inside the HARD 20-min train+score budget; sbatch --time=00:30:00 backstop wall. val_n stays 214 (score ALL L277 slices @ 321px detector-geometry FOV).
